title: Cross-border Data Exemption Request & Decision Log (Template)
body:
Purpose and scope:

This template is intended to standardize requests from product, solutions, or sales teams when a customer or integration requires an exception to Redwood Inference's default data residency or cross-border restrictions. It captures the business justification, risk assessment, mandatory compensating controls, decision rationale, and an auditable decision log to support compliance and future reviews.

How to use this document:
- Requestor fills Section A (Request summary) and Section B (Business justification).
- Requestor attaches any technical diagrams, customer statements of need, and contract excerpts (upload links to linked_artifacts).
- Security & Privacy perform initial risk assessment (Section C) and propose required controls (Section D).
- Legal reviews contract implications and DPA amendments required (Section E).
- Executive or Risk Committee approves or denies; decision recorded in Section F.

SECTION A — Request summary (to be completed by requestor)
1) Request ID: __________________ (auto-generated by tracker)
2) Requestor name / team: __________________
3) Customer / partner name: __________________
4) Product or integration: __________________
5) Date of request: __________________
6) Requested exception period: __________________ (temporary / permanent / until contract expiration)
7) Data types involved: 
   - PII (yes/no) _____  examples: names, emails
   - Customer content (yes/no) _____
   - Model inputs/outputs (yes/no) _____
   - Logs/telemetry (yes/no) _____
   - Derived features/metadata (yes/no) _____
8) Geographic flows requested: source region(s) -> destination region(s) (be specific)
9) Proposed architecture or path for cross-border transfer (short description + attach diagram link)

SECTION B — Business justification (requestor)
- Short statement of customer need (1–3 sentences):
  """
  """
- Why no existing configuration satisfies the need? (explain why region pinning, private deployment, or Dedicated cannot be used)
- Contractual/negotiation drivers (e.g., customer will not sign without this, RFP timeline constraint)
- Estimated revenue / strategic value (optional)
- Alternative mitigations proposed by the requestor (e.g., data minimization, synthetic data, partial redaction)

SECTION C — Initial Risk Assessment (security & privacy lead)
Checklist (mark risk level and explain):
- Sensitivity classification of data (Low / Medium / High / Very High) ____
- Likelihood of regulatory concern in destination jurisdiction (Low / Medium / High) ____
- Probability of reputational harm if leakage or non-compliance occurs (Low / Medium / High) ____
- Cross-border transfer legal basis required (e.g., SCCs, adequacy, contractual clause) : __________
- Potential breach impact (financial, legal, operational) summary: __________
- Any prior incidents relevant to the customer or integration: __________
- Timeline urgency: 
  - Required immediately for service launch (Y/N)
  - Can be delayed for technical rework (Y/N)
Notes / assessor comments: ___________________________

SECTION D — Mandatory compensating controls (security ops / infra)
Minimum baseline controls (must be satisfied for any approved exception):
- Data minimization: store only fields necessary; redact or truncate where possible (yes/no) ____
- Encryption: TLS 1.2+ in transit; AES-256 at rest (KMS-backed) ____
- Access control: RBAC limiting access to named service accounts and humans; MFA for admin access ____
- Key management: keys must be customer-specific or tenant-scoped; rotate per policy ____
- Logging & audit: detailed access logs retained for at least 1 year (or customer-requested period) and available for review ____
- Monitoring & alerting: abnormal access patterns alerting to SRE/Security ____
- Network controls: VPC peering, private links, IP allowlist, and no public egress for the data path ____
- Data segregation: physical or logical segregation of storage / compute for exceptional flows ____
- No backup replication outside approved regions without explicit approval ____
- Contractual safeguards: DPA clause amendment, liability caps, breach notification timelines specified ____
Additional controls recommended for High/Very High sensitivity data:
- HSM-backed key isolation, customer-managed keys (CMK) recommended
- On-prem or Dedicated deployment strongly preferred; if hosted, implement strict single-tenant routing
- Periodic third-party pen test or attestation for the integration

SECTION E — Legal & Contractual implications (legal lead)
Legal review checklist:
- Does the exception require a DPA amendment or specific Annex? (Y/N) If yes, reference draft: __________
- Is cross-border transfer mechanism in place? (SCCs, adequacy decision, explicit contractual transfer clause) 
- Does the exception trigger additional data subject rights handling requirements?
- Do licensing or model weight restrictions apply (e.g., export controls)?
- Indemnities and liability exposure assessment: notes and recommended limits
- Required customer representations / warranties (e.g., lawful basis for processing)
- Recommended clause language (attach redline link to linked_artifacts)

SECTION F — Decision and decision log (APPROVER completes)
Decision summary (one-line): APPROVE / DENY / APPROVE WITH CONDITIONS
Decision date: __________________
Approver name and title: __________________
Approver email: __________________
Decision rationale (short): __________________
Conditions imposed (if any): (list exact controls, timelines, remediation owners)
Approval expiration / review date (if temporary): __________________
If approved, record the deployment owner and runbook responsible for maintaining controls: __________________
If denied, recommended follow-up steps for product or sales (e.g., propose Dedicated, re-scope feature, propose alternate architecture)

Decision log (append each subsequent decision/review here)
- [YYYY-MM-DD] <Name> - <Decision> - <Notes / link to evidence/PR/patch>

SECTION G — Evidence & closure (ops owner)
List of proof items to attach before exception is considered operationally closed: (links or ticket ids)
- Architecture diagram link: __________
- Access control list snapshot: __________
- KMS key policy: __________
- Logging retention config: __________
- Executed DPA amendment or contract redline link: __________
- Pen test / attestation evidence (if required): __________
- Post-approval monitoring schedule and responsible SLIs/SLOs: __________

Retention and review cadence:
- All exception records must be retained for the longer of: the contract term + 3 years OR 7 years total.
- Exceptions with High/Very High sensitivity must be reviewed quarterly for first year and then semi-annually. Others should be reviewed annually.

Escalation and revocation:
- Any credible security incident related to the exception triggers immediate suspension of the exceptional flow and emergency review by SRE/Security/Legal.
- Approver(s) reserve the right to revoke an exception at any time; must record revocation in the decision log with rationale.

Appendix: example language for customer-facing DPA amendment (draft snippet)
1) Cross-border processing clause (example): 
"Notwithstanding the Data Residency Schedule, Processor may transfer and process Personal Data in [Approved Region(s)] for the purposes of performing the Services provided that Processor implements the controls and safeguards documented in the Cross-border Exception Approval attached as Exhibit A. Processor shall not transfer Customer Personal Data to jurisdictions outside the Approved Regions without prior written consent."

2) Audit & evidence clause (example): 
"Customer may request evidence of controls described in Exhibit A no more than twice per calendar year, with 30 days' notice. Evidence may be provided as redacted logs, attestation reports, or summary reports agreed with Processor."

Change history and template notes:
- v0.1 (2024-11-15) - initial draft by Ava Chen
- v0.2 (2024-12-04) - added legal checklist and evidence list (Priya Kapoor)
- v0.3 (2025-01-10) - tightened retention language and approval workflow (Diego Morales)

Open questions / known gaps (for program owners):
- Should we standardize a fixed list of evidence artifact formats? (e.g., CSV ACL exports, KMS policy JSON)
- Do we permit customer-managed keys for hosted customers as a default control for exceptions?
- How will exceptions be surfaced into the Console for telemetry/ops? (linked_ticket: JIRA-OPS-xxxx)

Contacts:
- Security & Privacy: security-privacy@redwood.ai
- Legal: contracts@redwood.ai
- Infrastructure / Ops: infra-ops@redwood.ai
- Product / Sales requestor: (see Section A)

-- end of template --
